subject: PAYMENT: Peak checkout failures — SDK header reassembly suspected
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@brightmart.com>

Cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@brightmart.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PAYMENT: peak window timeouts / 5xx spikes (urgent)

Hi Sean —

We just saw a severe spike in payment timeouts and 5xx errors between 08:45–09:05 PT during our morning promotional push. This impacted ~18% of checkout attempts (we sampled), causing visible cart drop and multiple customer complaints.

Attached are: brightmart_peak_logs_11-18.txt (server side error rates) and checkout_pcap_sample_11-18.pcap (tcp capture from our gateway).

Initial observation from our infra team: requests to your inference endpoint returned intermittent 502/503 and some responses were truncated mid-header which caused our HTTP client to fail fast. We capture header fragments in the PCAP.

We need a root cause and mitigation ASAP. This is directly hitting revenue — Tom and I are both on standby. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood SDK or gateway issue, and whether an emergency rollout is possible?

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Payments Engineering, BrightMart

Subject: Re: PAYMENT: peak window timeouts / 5xx spikes (urgent)

Quick findings from a first pass on the PCAP and our egress logs:
- We see multiple TCP segments where the HTTP headers get split across packets. In several traces the response header block is cutoff mid-field (e.g., truncated "Content-Length" and incomplete trailing CRLF sequences).
- Our edge logs show Connection: keep-alive clients sending pipelined requests; in a subset of flows the runtime's streaming dechunker returned an "incomplete headers" internal error before retry logic could run. Error code matches INF-3421 (we've seen similar in a lower-volume integration test last month).
- BrightMart is on SDK v2.3.1 (as Vanessa confirmed offline). That SDK contains an aggressive header coalescing heuristic that assumes header frames arrive contiguous; it doesn't robustly handle split header frames behind some HTTP proxies.

Short-term mitigation options:
1) Configure a temporary gateway-side timeout/backoff to avoid client retries collapsing into head-of-line blocking (low-friction, buys time).
2) Push an emergency patch to the SDK to make header reassembly tolerant to split frames (safe but requires customer clients to update).
3) Deploy a server-side acceptance fallback that treats a truncated header block as recoverable and attempts reassembly at the edge (requires a fast hotfix to the runtime).

I'm preparing a minimal runtime patch that tries (3) first — it will accept fragmented header blocks and attempt to reassemble with a small buffer window; this reduces immediate 5xx while we coordinate an SDK update. I estimate ~3 hours to validate and stage Canary.

I've attached an excerpt of the stacktrace and a short log summary (sdk_stacktrace_excerpt.txt).

I'll post a deeper analysis in 45 mins.

—Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: PAYMENT: peak window timeouts / 5xx spikes (urgent)

Thanks Priyom — that aligns with what our infra team saw. To confirm business impact: during the 20-minute window we lost ~6k checkouts and saw a 22% drop in completed payments for that promotion. We need a concrete mitigation and an ETA for code-level fix.

BrightMart preference: server-side fix first (so we don't have to immediately push new SDKs to all app versions). If you can get a Canary in front of our traffic in the next 3 hours we can route a sample (5%) to validate. Otherwise we will consider a short fallback to our legacy payment provider which hurts conversion.

Also — we will need a formal incident report and a committed timeline for an SDK release that fully addresses the reassembly heuristics.

Tom Becker

- We will produce an incident report (postmortem) within 48 hours and include mitigation steps and communication to customers.
